text:
sara: Quick follow-up from the authn/authz RFC — we need to finalize how we wire decision telemetry and runtime actor propagation. Two concrete asks: 1) which fields are required in the decision event (denied vs allowed), 2) how do we represent service vs user actors in the event model. tagging oncall/telemetry for ops tradeoffs.

jamie: For denied vs allowed: top-level decision, policy_id, matched_rule, and egress_scope. Keep PII out (no emails). Short and queriable.

ned: +1. Also include an actor_type enum: 'user'|'service'|'operator', and actor_id as a sha256 hash. Store raw ids only in internal TTLed audit store.

priya: Hashing works for prod observability but infra/debug often needs the real id. propose: hashed in high-volume telemetry, unhashed in internal only logs with strict TTL and access controls. :lock:

auth-bot: heads-up: audit pipeline currently samples ~1% of requests; we'll need to bump sampling for auth decisions. suggest tag `auth_decision` so pipeline can route.

sara: Tradeoffs: more logging increases cost and could impact SLOs. Oncall — thoughts on sampling vs full logging for denies?

karen: @oncall-rotation we should full-log all denies and any decision where policy tag == `elevated`. Sampling risks missing attacker patterns.

mike: ops viewpoint: full-log denies + 100% for token-exchange and admin endpoints. rest at 5% should be OK. Also push for a compact schema so queries are cheap.

sara: Draft schema (compact):

```
auth_event_v1 {
  decision: "allow"|"deny"
  policy_id: "string"
  rule_id: "string"
  actor_type: "user"|"service"|"operator"
  actor_hash: "sha256"
  resource: "string"
  scope: "org:123/project:456"
  reason: "string (nullable)"
  route: "/v1/generate"
  latency_ms: 12
}
```

jamie: also include `policy_cache_hit: true|false` so we can correlate auth latency with cache behavior and invalidate policy caches when debugging.

priya: on scoping: prefer explicit fields (`org_id`, `project_id`) rather than a single freeform scope string — makes filtering and RBAC audits way faster.

sara: agreed. also we need to be explicit about API key semantics: if an API key is project-scoped we log the project_id (not user email). add middleware config example: 

```
auth_middleware:
  propagate_actor: true
  propagate_fields: [actor_type, actor_hash, org_id, project_id, policy_id]
  mask_fields: [user_email]
```

ned: :thumbsup: i'll draft the RFC follow-up with schema, sampling rules, and retention policy. aim to ship PR by EOD tomorrow.

priya: i'll loop in legal & privacy for retention/TTL for unhashed ids.

sara: Thanks — filing follow-up RFC link (placeholder): https://rwd.internal/rfcs/1234. If nobody objects i'll lock on the schema and sampling rules tomorrow morning.
